# Where a usage pack's price comes from, and four ways to lower it: 18 October 2026

<!-- Generated by `node scripts/pack-cost-decomposition.mjs` from tests/pack-cost-decomposition-table.ts. Do not edit by hand: tests/pack-cost-decomposition.test.ts fails when this file is stale. -->

**An analysis for the owner, not a change.** No price, limit, gate or tax assumption in code changes with it, and `PLANS_ON_SALE` stays false. Every figure is computed by the repository's own margin code (lib/receiving-costs.ts `unitUnder`, `receivingOf`, `costBudgetCents`, under the sizing reading; tests/pricing-usage-proposal-table.ts `PACKS`, `packPriceCents`, `atScale`, `linePriceCents`); none is typed. It takes apart the packs of docs/pricing-usage-proposal-2026-10-18.md.

## The short answer

The list-email pack sells 2,500 list emails for $62: 27.56× the $2.25 the emails cost. That multiplier is four factors that multiply back to it exactly:

| Factor | What it is | List-email pack | Share of the multiplier (by logarithm) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. The 60% floor and the 27.5% profit tax | Net must be 60% after a 27.5% tax, so pretax profit must be 82.76% of revenue and every cost together at most 17.24% | 5.81× | 53% |
| 2. The fee's and the reserves' percentages | 6.6% of the amount charged (the price plus the buyer's 27% tax on top), 1.5% remittance, 1% refund reserve, 1% of the amount charged as dispute reserve | 3.43× | 37% |
| 3. The fixed cents of one payment | the fee's 30¢ and the dispute reserve's 1% of $30 | 1.24× | 6% |
| 4. A whole-dollar price and the add-on's 25¢ of room | what the price leaves unused | 1.12× | 3% |
| **Price over cost** | | **27.56×** | 100% |

Factors 1 and 2 together are 19.94×: the "twenty times" of the proposal, and the floor no pack size can go under. Factor 1 alone is the owner's rule (60% after at least 27.5%): it makes any cost cost 5.81× in price. Factor 2 is the receiving model shared with Hazelsong. **The email itself is 3.63% of the pack's price; the supplier's rate is not what makes the pack dear.**

## The structure, on $100 with nothing used

Under the sizing reading (the buyer's tax on top at 27%, remittance 1.5%, at least 27.5% on profit), a $100 payment on its own:

| Line | $100 payment |
| --- | --- |
| Charged to the buyer (the price plus the tax on top) | $127.00 |
| The dearer provider's fee | $8.70 |
| Remittance | $1.50 |
| Refund reserve | $1.00 |
| Dispute reserve | $1.57 |
| Every cost the 60% floor and the profit tax allow | $17.24 |
| Left for the use itself | $4.47 |

So a dollar of use needs about $22.37 of price at this size, and about 19.72× at any size once the fixed cents are spread thin.

Every column but the unused room adds up to the price: use, fee, remittance, reserves and tax are the unit's costs, and the net is what is left. The unused room is part of the net: what the whole-dollar price leaves above 60%, the add-on's 25¢ included.

- **Of the fee and the dispute reserve, what is charged on the buyer's tax added on top**: visits $0.92, orders $0.73, list-email $1.30, ai $1.06, storage $0.89, video $0.52. The providers charge their percentages on the whole amount the buyer pays, 27% more than the price at the worst.
- **Free-account share: none.** A pack's own payment carries none of the stores that pay nothing; their share (line free-share, 1/40 of a free store's worst window) is in each plan's own payment. Selling packs to stores whose plan carries that share leaves it where it is.
- **Sales tax on top** is not revenue and not a cost of its own here: it is collected for the state and passed on; what it costs is the fee and dispute reserve charged on it, in the line above.

The four factors, for every pack:

| Pack | Floor and tax | Percentages | Fixed cents | Whole dollar and room | Price over cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5,000 visits | 5.80× | 3.43× | 1.37× | 1.18× | **32.35×** |
| 250 orders, with their access and store emails | 5.80× | 3.47× | 1.53× | 1.28× | **39.33×** |
| 2,500 list emails | 5.81× | 3.43× | 1.24× | 1.12× | **27.56×** |
| 20 AI writing jobs and 100 answers | 5.80× | 3.43× | 1.31× | 1.19× | **31.25×** |
| 25 GB of storage | 5.80× | 3.45× | 1.39× | 1.20× | **33.33×** |
| 20 video hours watched | 5.81× | 3.50× | 2.03× | 2.00× | **82.76×** |

The smaller the cost of a pack's use, the larger factors 3 and 4: the video pack's use is so small that its fixed cents and its rounding nearly double its price.

## Option 1: a line on the renewal invoice

The same amount added to the store's next renewal invoice instead of its own payment: it pays only the fee's percentages (no fixed fee, no dispute fees of its own: the invoice's own plan unit reserves those), but it is used before it is paid.

| Pack | As its own prepaid payment | As a line on the renewal | Per unit as a line | Net as a line | Lost if the invoice is never paid | The same, ten times the amount: line price, per unit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5,000 visits | $44 | $33 | $6.60 per 1,000 visits | 60.63% | $1.36 | $272, $5.44 per 1,000 visits |
| 250 orders, with their access and store emails | $35 | $24 | $0.10 per order | 60.87% | $0.89 | $179, $0.07 per order |
| 2,500 list emails | $62 | $50 | $20.00 per 1,000 emails | 60.36% | $2.25 | $448, $17.92 per 1,000 emails |
| 20 AI writing jobs and 100 answers | $50 | $37 | $1.85 per writing job with 5 answers | 60.48% | $1.60 | $319, $1.60 per writing job with 5 answers |
| 25 GB of storage | $43 | $32 | $1.28 per GB | 60.71% | $1.29 | $258, $1.03 per GB |
| 20 video hours watched | $24 | $11 | $0.55 per hour | 61.63% | $0.29 | $63, $0.32 per hour |

It removes factor 3 only, and only the pack's own fixed cents, so the email line is $20.00 a thousand instead of $24.80. In exchange it creates the non-payment exposure of AGENTS.md ("funded exposures"): use that happened before an invoice that is never paid. Its bound, per store and per window:

- **A ceiling on what may be used before payment.** The window's figure can rise past the plan's by at most a set amount (one pack's worth, say); the meters that refuse past a plan's figure today (lib/email.ts, lib/traffic.ts, lib/order-admission.ts, lib/ai-spend.ts, lib/storage-quota.ts, lib/video-admission-rules.ts) would refuse past that ceiling the same way. A store whose last invoice is unpaid gets no ceiling until it pays.
- **Its cost per case** is the use's cost at that ceiling (the column above: $2.25 for 2,500 list emails), and no fee, because a failed invoice charges none. It must be entered under the `non_payment` scope of the funded-exposure review (lib/funded-exposure-rules.ts) with a maximum number of cases a month, and paid from the reviewed company exposure ceiling added to the fixed costs, which raises the minimum paying base.
- **A card pre-authorization** would bound it by a hold instead; how long a hold lasts at Stripe was not read today, and a window lasts up to 31 days, so it is not evaluated here.
- **What must be built:** the ceiling above each window's figure, invoice items added to the renewal invoice at Stripe, pausing the ceiling on `past_due`, the exposure review's `non_payment` case with its count, and the terms.

A larger pack asks the buyer to commit a larger sum to one resource, and every pack is used in full only in the worst case the owner's rule prices: the buyer who uses less pays the same. Nothing new has to be built beyond the packs themselves.

## Option 3: prepaid credits bought in larger amounts

A credit balance bought on its own payment and spent on any of the six resources, each at one rate: its unit cost times the multiplier the amount allows (its room for use, less the add-on's 25¢), rounded up to the cent. However it is spent, its use costs at most what spending it all on one resource costs, and that worst case is held to 60%.

| Credit bought | Price over cost | Per 1,000 visits | Per order | Per 1,000 emails | Per writing job with 5 answers | Per GB | Per hour | Net, the whole credit on its dearest-to-serve resource |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $50 | 30.12× | $8.17 | $0.11 | $27.11 | $2.40 | $1.55 | $0.44 | 60.36% |
| $100 | 23.70× | $6.43 | $0.09 | $21.33 | $1.89 | $1.22 | $0.35 | 60.18% |
| $250 | 21.11× | $5.73 | $0.08 | $19.01 | $1.69 | $1.09 | $0.31 | 60.07% |
| $500 | 20.35× | $5.52 | $0.08 | $18.32 | $1.63 | $1.05 | $0.30 | 60.03% |
| $1,000 | 19.98× | $5.42 | $0.08 | $17.99 | $1.60 | $1.03 | $0.29 | 60.01% |

Each rate column is per the unit its pack prints (per 1,000 visits, per order with its emails, per 1,000 list emails, per writing job with 5 answers, per GB of storage for a window and its closing days, per video hour watched).

Credits do what larger packs do without asking the buyer to guess which resource they will need, and they stay prepaid: nothing is used before it is paid, so no non-payment exposure. What they need besides the packs:

- a balance per store, taken before each use the way the window's figures are taken today, and refused when empty (each meter would draw on the plan's figure first and the balance after);
- a fixed life for a credit (say twelve months), because an unused balance is an obligation; a refund only while none of it was used (Hazelsong's rule for packs), so the 14-day money-back refund's funded exposure (docs/funded-exposure-review.md) is unchanged in kind;
- an optional automatic top-up when the balance runs low (HighLevel's wallet does this), each top-up its own prepaid payment at the same rates;
- the AI ceiling's company total (`companyMicroUsd`) counting what credits buy, as the proposal already says for packs.

## Option 4: the supplier rates that could be lower, if built

**List email through Amazon SES only.** lib/email.ts already sends through SES whenever Amazon allows it and falls back to Resend otherwise, which is why every email is priced at Resend's $0.90. `sendBatch` already takes `only: "amazon"` and answers "retry" when Amazon cannot take the batch. If emails bought in a pack went only through SES and waited when it is down, their cost would be SES's dearest listed rate, $0.23 a thousand (the Enterprise plan; à la carte is $0.10), not $0.90:

| List emails | At Resend's $0.90 (today): price, per 1,000 | At SES's $0.23, SES only: price, per 1,000 | Net at SES |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2,500 | $62, $24.80 | $29, $11.60 | 60.65% |
| 10,000 | $195, $19.50 | $64, $6.40 | 60.37% |
| 25,000 | $460, $18.40 | $131, $5.24 | 60.15% |
| 100,000 | $1,786, $17.86 | $470, $4.70 | 60.04% |

What must be built: the pack's emails sent with `only: "amazon"` and held, not handed to Resend, while Amazon is down or out of its day; the pack's figure counting only what SES took; no attachments on list emails, or their $0.12 a GB counted; and the page saying pack emails can wait. The order pack's access and store emails must not wait (a buyer is owed their access), so they stay at Resend's rate.

**Storage in R2 only.** A storage pack that raises only the room for sold files (lib/vault.ts, R2 at $0.015) would cost $34 for 25 GB of storage instead of $43 (net 60.52%). It is honest only if the code proves those bytes are in R2; the storage figure today counts a store's files in every store they may be in, at the dearest.

No other unit cost can be lowered from its own page: visits, the database and AI are priced at their published rates, and video may be low (above).

## The one structural option that does the most

**Prepaid credits bought in larger amounts (option 3).** It is the only option that lowers factors 3 and 4 for every resource at once while staying prepaid: no non-payment exposure to fund (option 1 adds one and saves only the fixed cents), and no bet by the buyer on one resource (option 2). At $250 a credit buys list email at $19.01 a thousand, at $1,000 $17.99, against $24.80 in the proposal's pack; every other resource falls the same way (table above). Its floor is factors 1 and 2, about 19.94× a unit's cost, which no structure removes while the 60% rule and the receiving model stand.

For email specifically the larger lever is the supplier, not the structure: sending what a credit buys through Amazon SES alone (option 4) takes the $1,000 credit's rate to $4.60 a thousand. Even so it stays 6.81× HighLevel's rate: a creator who sends a lot of email will still compare it with ClickFunnels' and Kajabi's allowances.

## What this does not decide

- **The rule and the receiving model.** Factor 1 is the owner's 60% after at least 27.5%; factor 2 is the receiving model the two products share (lib/receiving-costs.ts, aligned with Hazelsong's). Neither is changed or questioned here; under the most-tax reading (the gate) no pack and no option keeps 60%, exactly as today.
- **Stripe's own page was not read today** (the fetch was refused), so nothing is said about which of its surcharges a pack's payment would really pay. The model keeps the dearer of Stripe's 6.6% + 30¢ and Paddle's 5% + 50¢ either way.
- **Demand.** Whether creators buy credits, at which amounts, and how much of what they buy they use: unknown until a sale is open. Every net above is at full use, the owner's rule.
- **The order of building.** Credits need the packs' machinery first (a Stripe charge, a balance, the meters drawing on it, the pages and terms); SES-only routing needs the pack's figure and the waiting path. Nothing here builds either.
